rot.title: Rotary
rot.onTip: For round items (tumblers, bottles, pens). You draw on the unrolled surface: X = along the item, Y = around it.
rot.axisTip: Y connector: the rotary is plugged in instead of the Y motor (xTool RA2, Creality, LaserPecker, most roller rotaries). A axis: its own 4th axis (grblHAL, FluidNC), Y stays still.
rot.diaTip: Outer diameter where you engrave. This gives the circumference.
rot.rollerTip: Diameter of the driven roller. The item turns as far as the roller rolls.
rot.mprTip: Y travel for one full turn of the roller or chuck. Test: jog 100 mm in Y and count how far the roller turns.
rot.info: Circumference {c} mm (Ø {d} mm) – the blue band on the bed
rot.hint: Place the design in the blue band; the origin (Y = 0) is where the laser is when you start. The simulation shows the unrolled surface.
rot.outside: {n} part(s) lie outside the circumference ({c} mm) – they would overlap.
rot.arcs: Rotary: the G-code contains arcs – they cannot be converted.
rot.simFlat: [Rotary] The simulation shows the unrolled surface (not converted). To see it all around: 3D preview in the Laser tab.
sl.title: Shape library
sl.hint: Click a shape – it is placed in the centre of the bed at the chosen width. Then move, rotate and edit it like any other shape (e.g. with “Edit points”).
tip.cmd.shapeLib: Shape library: insert ready-made shapes (heart, star, tag, gear …)
tip.cmd.nameGen: Name generator: a name as one connected lettering to cut out in one piece
ngen.title: Name generator
ng.title: Node graph
ng.desc: The name becomes one part that can be cut out in one piece. The preview shows right away whether everything is connected.
ng.tpl.name: Lettering
ng.doneLayer: Backing and lettering inserted as two parts ({w} × {h} mm) – the lettering lies above, e.g. cut it from another material and glue it on
ng.openFont: The single-line font has no areas – please choose another font.
ng.pieces: Note: {n} separate pieces – reduce the letter spacing or choose baseline or outline.
eng.curveHint: Click = add point, drag = bend brightness, double-click = delete point. Left = dark areas, right = light. Behind it the brightness distribution.
tile.title: Split into tiles
tile.desc: The design ({w} × {h} mm) is split into pieces that fit on the machine one by one. Areas and lines are cut at the tile borders, images are split.
tile.beds: Each tile on its own bed (at the origin)
tile.marks: Registration marks in the corners (for aligning)
tile.select: First select the design you want to split.
tile.tooMany: Too many tiles (over 400) – make the tiles bigger.
tile.imageRotated: [Tiles] A rotated image is not split; it goes whole into the tile of its centre.
tile.doneBeds: [Tiles] {n} tiles, each on its own bed. Work through them bed by bed and line the pieces up with the registration marks.
tip.cmd.tiles: Split into tiles: cut a large design into pieces that fit on the bed (each tile on its own bed)
v3d.title: 3D view – how it will look
v3d.carveEmpty: No cutter goes below Z = 0 in the G-code – nothing to remove.
v3d.carveThrough: cut through at {t} mm material thickness
v3d.hint: Left drag = turn in every direction · right drag or Shift = move · wheel = zoom · double-click = reset. Preview only – engraving as surface, cuts go through the full thickness.
v3d.hintCarve: Left drag = rotate · right drag or Shift = pan · wheel = zoom · double-click = reset. Calculated from the real G-code with the shape of every cutter – you see pockets, V-carving and material left in inside corners. Deeper than the thickness = cut through.
v3d.noGl: The 3D view needs WebGL – it is not available here.
v3d.noCut: Nothing is cut out – {t} mm sheet with engraving
tip.cmd.view3d: 3D view: look at the cut-out parts in wood, acrylic … from all sides (with rotary: the round item)
tip.cmd.stlExport: STL for 3D printing: save the selection as a 3D solid (height per layer, engraving as recess or relief)
stlx.title: STL for 3D printing
stl.descSel: {n} selected shapes become one 3D solid. Cut-outs and holes stay open. Choose what each group becomes.
stl.descAll: All {n} shapes become one 3D solid. Cut-outs and holes stay open. Choose what each group becomes.
stl.kindHint: Base body: the part gets this tall. Recess: the area is sunk this deep into the base body. Relief: the area stands out this far above the base body. Mouse in the preview: drag = rotate, wheel = zoom.
stl.empty: Nothing to print – set at least one group to base body or relief.
stl.none: No closed shapes for the STL file – draw or select something first.
tip.cmd.nodeGraph: Node graph – build workflows from blocks
ng.hint: Drag an output (right) onto an input (left). Drag the empty area to move, wheel = zoom, Del = delete node, click a wire = remove it.
ng.applyTip: Places the result of every output node on the bed (replaces its previous result)
ng.noSel: Click a node to change its settings.
ng.takeNone: Select shapes or an image on the bed first, then click “Take selection”.
ng.applied: [Node graph] {n} shape(s) placed on the bed.
ng.nothing: [Node graph] The output is empty – nothing placed.
ng.d.source: Takes the selected shapes and/or image from the bed as a copy.
ng.d.rect: A rectangle, optionally with rounded corners.
ng.d.circle: A circle with the given diameter.
ng.d.number: A number you can connect to green inputs of several nodes.
ng.d.math: Adds, subtracts, multiplies or divides two numbers.
ng.d.transform: Moves, rotates, scales or mirrors the shapes (around their centre).
ng.d.place: Puts the shapes at a fixed position on the bed (mm).
ng.d.offset: Outline at a distance – outwards, inwards or both.
ng.d.boolean: Union, subtract (A minus B), intersection or exclusion of closed shapes.
ng.d.array: Copies the shapes in columns and rows.
ng.d.pattern: Fills the area with copies of the motif.
ng.d.nest: Packs the parts tightly onto the bed.
ng.d.tiles: Splits a large design into tiles – each tile on its own bed if you like.
ng.d.layer: Sets the laser layer, cut side and depth.
ng.d.merge: Puts up to three shape lists together.
ng.d.bgRemove: Removes the light background around the subject.
ng.d.curve: Makes shadows, midtones or highlights lighter or darker.
ng.d.adjust: Brightness, contrast, gamma, sharpening and invert.
ng.d.engrave: Dithering method and line interval for the laser.
ng.d.imgSize: Width in mm (height follows) and position of the lower-left corner.
ng.d.mask: Engraves the image only inside the closed shapes.
ng.d.output: Whatever arrives here goes onto the bed with “Place on bed”.
ng.p.toBeds: Each tile on its own bed
ng.p.removeSrc: Remove the originals from the bed
ng.w.takeFirst: Select something on the bed, then “Take selection”
ng.w.nestFailed: {n} part(s) did not fit on the bed
ng.w.tileImage: Images are not split here – use the Tiles button on the toolbar
ng.p.live: Live: follow changes on the bed
ng.tpl.title: Templates
ng.tpl.noOwn: No own templates yet – enter a name below and save.
ng.tpl.hint: Templates keep only the workflow, not the shapes taken from the bed – so they fit any design. The project file saves the whole graph.
ng.tpl.confirmLoad: Replace the current graph with “{name}”? Shapes already taken from the bed are kept.
ng.tpl.full: [Node graph] Could not save the template (storage full).
ng.tpl.badFile: [Node graph] This is not a CNC Craft node graph file.
ng.tpl.sign.d: Rounded rectangle 120 × 60 mm minus two 6 mm holes for hanging.
ng.tpl.slate.d: For dark material: inverted, lighter midtones, fine dithering. Take a photo from the bed first.
ng.tpl.photoRound.d: Background removed, 80 mm wide, engraved only inside a 76 mm circle that is also cut out.
ng.tpl.nest.d: Packs the taken parts tightly onto the bed and replaces the originals.
ng.tpl.tiles.d: Splits the taken design into 300 × 300 mm tiles, each on its own bed.
rot.aBlocked: Rotary: the {fw} controller has no A axis – the A values would be ignored and everything would be engraved on one line. Choose “Y connector” and plug the rotary into the Y port.
rot.aNoAxis: Rotary: the board reports no settings for a 4th axis ($103 is missing). Plain GRBL then stops with error 20 – you need grblHAL, FluidNC or Grbl_ESP32 with an A axis, or the Y connector.
rot.ruidaOwn: Rotary on Ruida: CNC Craft already converts Y. Switch the rotary function in the controller off (panel or RDWorks “Rotary” setting), otherwise it is converted twice and the design comes out stretched.
rot.aNote: A axis only works with grblHAL, FluidNC or Grbl_ESP32 boards that have a 4th axis – not with Ruida, K40 or Marlin. Those use the Y connector.
fly.shapes: Shapes: line, rectangle, ellipse, polygon, arc
fly.extras: Extras: nesting, box generator, shape library, material test grid, QR code, serial numbers, 3D view, node graph
fly.combine: Combine: union, subtract, intersect, split, weld & score
fly.edit: Edit: offset, round corners, pattern fill, fix centre, tiles, split into parts
rp.noSel: Nothing selected – click a shape to set its size, position, cut side and tabs.
box.tdesc.traylid: Sorting box with dividers and a two-part lid; the dividers are one material thickness lower so the lid fits.
box.tdesc.flexcup: Like the round box, without lid – for pens, brushes or tools. Bottom and ring keep the shape, puzzle seam at the back.
box.tdesc.lantern: Closed box with arched windows in all four walls and a vent hole in the lid – for tea lights or LED candles. Glue paper or thin acrylic behind the windows if you like.
box.tdesc.coin: Closed box with a coin slot in the lid (fits up to a 2-euro coin) and a round hole in the bottom with a plug of two discs: glue the small disc under the big one, it holds in the hole.
pr.guardNoStop: [Probing] The probe reported contact but the machine kept moving – stopped immediately (hold + reset). Probing only stops by itself while measuring slowly downwards; when it moves up or to the sensor, do not touch the probe. If it also happens while probing: the board does not evaluate the probe input (pin assignment / firmware).
pr.guardWrongDir: [Probing] Z moved UP while probing downwards – stopped immediately. Check the Z direction: jog Z− must move the spindle down; otherwise flip the Z bit in $3 (direction invert).
pr.unlockHint: [Probing] After the stop the machine is locked – check, then 🔓 Unlock (or F11).
pr.phaseSearch: [Probing] Moving down slowly to find contact (max. {mm} mm) …
pr.phaseMeasure: [Probing] Contact – 2 mm up, measuring again slowly …
pr.phaseTravel: [Probing] Moving to the sensor X {x} / Y {y} (do not touch the probe now) …
pr.sensorNotSet: [Probing] Set the sensor position first: move the spindle exactly above the sensor and click “Use current position”.
pr.liveTip: What the board reports for the probe input right now. Touch the clamp to the bit: it must switch to “contact”. If not, the board does not see the probe – check wiring and pin.
pr.liftMax: [Probing] Lift is limited to {mm} mm – more usually runs into the Z limit switch.
pr.phaseNoLift: [Probing] Z is already at the top – going straight to the sensor.
pr.unstable: [Probing] The two measurements do not match ({a} / {b} mm, machine Z) – the probe signal is unreliable (interference?). Z was NOT set.
pr.glitch: [Probing] Interference pulse at Z {z} mm ignored (probe open again) – searching on …
pr.tooManyGlitches: [Probing] More than 25 interference pulses – stopped, Z was NOT set. The probe input picks up a lot of interference (cable along the motor cables?).
box.type.scoop: Index box / tray with finger notch
box.tdesc.tissue: Closed box with a long opening with round ends in the lid – size it to fit your tissue pack (inner dimensions help).
box.tdesc.bird: Closed box with an entrance hole (up to 32 mm, for tits) high in the front, small vent holes in the sides and drain holes in the bottom. Use untreated wood; glue the lid on only at the back or hinge it so you can clean it.
box.tdesc.planter: Open box with drain holes (6 mm) in the bottom. For wood: line the inside with foil or seal it, then it lasts much longer.
box.tdesc.scoop: Open box with a half-round finger notch at the top of the front – for index cards, notes, tools or as a desk tray.
mand.title: Mandala generator
mand.desc: Round disc with patterns in rings, the same all around – to cut with laser or router. Every click on “New pattern” gives a different mandala.
mand.engrave: Only engrave the patterns (don't cut them out)
mand.hint: Bridge width = smallest distance between two holes and to the edge – keeps the part in one piece. Router: choose bridge width and smallest holes bigger than the cutter Ø. Laser: from about 1.5 mm for 3 mm wood.
mand.done: [Mandala] Created with {n} patterns (selected as a group).
mand.bigger: [Mandala] Ø {d} mm is bigger than the bed – please move it or make it smaller.
eng.autoGentleTip: Natural look: stretch the tones, balance the midtones, a little local contrast and sharpening
eng.autoStrongTip: More contrast and detail – brings out fur, hair and fine structures (good for wood and slate)
eng.autoDoneStrong: [Image] Auto enhanced (strong): more contrast, strong local contrast for fine detail, bright edges are held back.
rp.modeVcarveTip: Carve the area with a V-bit: the further from the edge, the deeper – sharp edges and pointed corners (lettering, signs). Depth = maximum depth, deeper parts get a flat bottom
rp.modeDrillTip: Drill holes: straight down in the centre of each selected shape (circles, small outlines), with chip breaking – after every depth per pass of the tool it comes fully out and goes back in. Best with a drill bit of the hole size. Holes are drilled first, on the shortest route.
rp.modeFaceTip: Face the surface: the bounding rectangle of the shape is milled flat in rows down to the milling depth (e.g. stock, spoilboard). Rows run past the edge, plunging happens next to it. Best with a face mill.
ops.title: Operations
ops.addTip: Another operation for this shape, e.g. first pocket, then chamfer, then cut out – each with its own tool and depth.
ops.forTip: The selection has different types (e.g. outline and holes of a part). Choose here which ones the operations apply to – e.g. only the holes get a chamfer.
ops.scope: Applies to all {n} selected shapes (they get the same list).
ops.firstTip: First operation = the shape itself: type above under "Cut side", tool and depth as before.
ops.cwTip: How wide the chamfer gets at the top edge. CNC Craft calculates the depth from the angle of the chamfer or V-bit.
ops.assignTip: Choose one tool per operation type – e.g. pockets with the 6 mm cutter, cut-outs with the 3 mm cutter, chamfers with the 90° chamfer bit.
ops.assignDescSel: For the {n} selected shapes: choose the tool per operation type.
ops.assignDescAll: For all {n} shapes of the design: choose the tool per operation type.
rp.inlayTip: Make a V-carve inlay from the selection: pocket + mirrored plug from a second wood that fits exactly
gcw.vNeedsVbit: Shape {n}: V-carve/inlay needs a V-bit with an angle – choose one in the tool picker (skipped).
gcw.vEmpty: Shape {n}: no V-carve paths – are the contours closed?
gcw.vFlat: Shape {n}: V-carve reaches the depth limit ({d} mm) – the wide parts get a flat bottom carved with the V-bit (slow; for large areas clear with an end mill first).
inlay.selectFirst: Inlay: select closed shapes first (e.g. text or a heart).
inlay.title: V-carve inlay
inlay.desc: The selection becomes the pocket. A mirrored copy is placed next to it as the plug – mill it from a second wood with the same V-bit.
inlay.info: Pocket: {p} mm deep · plug: start depth {s} mm, walls down to {w} mm
inlay.howto: Then: glue the plug upside down into the pocket, clamp it, and cut or plane off the rest of the plug board. The plug board must be at least as thick as the wall depth mm thick.
inlay.done: [Inlay] {n} shape(s) → V-carve pocket {p} mm deep; mirrored plug placed to the right (start depth {s} mm). Use a V-bit for both.
c3d.openTip: Mill the model as a 3D shape (relief, bowl): rough in layers, then finish with a ball end mill
c3d.title: 3D milling – relief and freeform from the model
c3d.marginTip: The cutter also goes around the model down to the bottom. Off: only inside the model area.
c3d.finishStepHint: Without roughing, the cutter finishes in layers with this step down from top to bottom.
c3d.toolHint: Ball and flat end mills are calculated exactly. Other types are calculated like a flat end mill – that may leave some material but never cuts too deep. The top of the model is at Z 0 (top of material).
c3d.hintView: Position of the model on the bed. After calculating: milling result from the G-code.
c3d.result: {n} paths · roughing {r} m · finishing {f} m · approx. {min} min
c3d.noTools: No cutters in the tool list – please add one under “Tools” first.
c3d.noOp: Please turn on roughing or finishing.
c3d.done: 3D milling: {n} paths calculated, G-code with {l} lines.
c3d.needApp: 3D milling is calculated in the app core – this only works in the installed app, not in the browser.
c3d.warnThick: The model is taller than the material – the cutter will go through the bottom.
c3d.warnFlute: {name}: flute length {l} mm is shorter than the model height {h} mm.
c3d.loaded: 3D milling: G-code loaded as job ({n} lines).
c3d.gcRough: 3D roughing: stock to leave {a} mm, step down {z} mm
face.btnTip: Face both sides of the stock by the same amount first – against warping when the 3D job removes a lot of material.
face.title: Face stock on both sides
face.intro: Wood, plastics and aluminium have internal stresses. If the 3D job removes a lot of material from one side only, the part warps. So face both sides by the same amount first. Best make the area as big as the whole plate.
face.depthTip: This much is taken off the top – and again on the other side after flipping.
face.info: {n} depth(s), {r} rows, approx. {m} min per side.
face.invalid: Check the values – area, removal and step down must be greater than 0.
face.warnThin: ⚠ Afterwards the material is thinner than the model ({h} mm) – remove less or use thicker material.
face.step1: Load the job, zero Z on the top surface and mill side 1.
face.step2: Flip the plate (same corner against the stop), clamp it, zero Z on the new top surface.
face.step3: Mill the same job again – side 2.
face.step4: Then load the 3D job again (Z on the top surface). The material thickness has already been adjusted.
face.noTool: [Facing] Create a tool in the library first.
face.gcHead: CNC Craft - facing stock: {d} mm per side, area {w} x {h} mm
face.loaded: [Facing] Job loaded: {d} mm per side. Mill side 1, flip, zero Z again, start once more.
face.spoil.title: Surface the spoilboard
face.spoil.intro: Mills the spoilboard (or another surface) flat – so every workpiece lies flat and at the same depth again. The whole bed is suggested; position and size count from the work zero.
face.spoil.step1: Set X/Y zero at the bottom left of the bed, zero Z on the top of the spoilboard.
face.spoil.step2: Load the job and mill it – best with your largest face mill, dust extraction on.
face.spoil.step3: Then vacuum and check: if some spots were missed, surface again with a small removal.
face.spoil.loaded: [Facing] Job loaded: surface spoilboard by {d} mm.
face.spoil.millOnly: [Facing] Surfacing the spoilboard only works in router mode.
tc.noSwitch: Tool change in progress – finish or cancel it first, then switch machines.
tc.title: Tool change (M6 / M0)
tc.modeTip: What happens when the job stops for a tool change: manual (just a notice), fixed tool length sensor (measures automatically) or mobile touch plate (you place it, CNC Craft probes).
tc.safeTip: Z moves up to this height in machine coordinates during the change (after homing the top is usually 0, so e.g. −2). It only moves up, never down.
tc.liftTip: Where Z goes when the job stops for a tool change (also in “Manual” mode). “Height above work zero” works on every machine. “All the way up” moves to just below the limit switch (only with homing; otherwise the height above work zero is used). “Safe height” is a machine coordinate (only meaningful with homing). “Don't lift” only applies to “Manual”. Before continuing, the machine moves back to where it was.
tc.workZTip: Z moves up to this height above the workpiece zero (Z 0) – e.g. 40 mm leaves room for a 19 mm touch plate. Works without homing. With homing it never goes higher than just below the limit switch. It only moves up, never down.
tc.log.noTop: [Tool change] “All the way up” needs homing upwards ($22 on) – using {z} mm above work zero instead
tc.err.lift: [Tool change] Could not lift Z ({e}) – please move it up yourself.
tc.travelTip: Z searches down at most this far. No contact → abort, Z is NOT changed.
tc.szTip: Above the sensor, move down quickly to this height before the slow search. Choose it high enough for your longest tool! Same as the safe height (or higher) = search from the top.
tc.posTip: Where you change the tool: where the job stopped, or at a fixed change position (e.g. front centre).
tc.xTip: Change position X in machine coordinates (mm)
tc.yTip: Change position Y in machine coordinates (mm)
tc.hereTip: Move the machine to where you can easily reach the spindle, then click here.
tc.hereDone: Change position saved: X {x}, Y {y} (machine coordinates).
tc.feedTip: Speed of the moves to the sensor, to the change position and back.
tc.reuseSensor: Taken from above: sensor position X {x} / Y {y}, search {f} mm/min, measure {sl} mm/min.
tc.reusePlate: Taken from above: plate thickness {d} mm, search {f} mm/min, measure {sl} mm/min.
tc.refNone: Reference: none yet – at the first change the old tool is measured first.
tc.refSet: Reference: contact at machine Z {z} (tool in the spindle).
tc.refGoTip: Measures the tool currently in the spindle on the sensor. The Z zero is not changed.
tc.m6Tip: Write “M6 T2” instead of just “M0” at tool changes. CNC Craft stops at both. Note: GRBL 1.1 itself does not know M6 (error 20) – send such files only with CNC Craft or to grblHAL.
tc.refConfirm:
Measure the tool in the spindle on the sensor?

Z moves up, then to the sensor (X {x}, Y {y}) and probes. Keep a finger on the E-stop!
tc.log.safe: [Tool change] Z up to machine Z {z}
tc.log.ref: [Tool change] No reference yet – measuring the old tool on the sensor first.
tc.log.delta: [Tool change] Length difference {d} mm – Z zero adjusted.
tc.log.refDone: Reference measured: contact at machine Z {z}.
tc.err.ref: The old tool could not be measured.
tc.err.measure: Measurement failed – Z was not changed. Check cable and clamp, then try again.
tc.err.step: Step failed ({e}) – the job is ended.
tc.useDialog: Tool change in progress – please continue in the “Tool change” window.

Continue without measuring?

Only if you zeroed Z yourself – otherwise the new tool cuts at the wrong depth.
dr.onTip: Against thermal drift: spindle and Z axis expand during long jobs, so the machine cuts a little deeper or shallower. When on, the job stops at safe points (between two shapes, cutter up), measures the tool again and shifts Z by the difference to the first measurement. With a fixed sensor this runs by itself, with the hand probe at the tool change position. Applies to newly generated G-code. Default: off.
dr.minTip: Time between two measurements (estimated run time). The first measurement at the start of the job is the reference.
dr.howSensor: Measured on the fixed sensor (X {x}, Y {y}) – no action needed.
dr.howPlate: Measured with the hand probe at the tool change position (X {x}, Y {y}): put the plate there, on a surface that is not milled (e.g. spoilboard) – always the same spot and the same plate.
dr.howNoSpot: ⚠ With a hand probe, re-measuring needs a fixed spot: set the “tool change position” above.
dr.sub: Regular measurement every {m} min – Z is corrected by the difference.
dr.st.parking: Spindle off, Z moves to safe height …
dr.st.travel: Moving to the measuring spot (tool change position) …
dr.st.waitPlate: Put the probe plate on the measuring spot (same spot as for the first measurement), clip on the cutter. Lower Z with the jog buttons if needed (searches at most {travel} mm). Then “Probe”.
dr.st.waitRemove: Measured. Now remove the probe plate and clip and confirm.
dr.st.waitResume: Done. Check that everything is clear, then “Resume job”.
dr.st.aborted: Cancelled – the job will NOT continue.
dr.skipConfirm:
Continue milling without correction?

Z stays as it is.
dr.resDelta: Difference since the first measurement: {d} mm (Z zero corrected).
dr.tooBig: Difference of {d} mm is unusually large (more than {max} mm) – chip on the sensor or wrong spot? Measure again or continue without correction.

tc.log.stayHigh: [Tool change] The cutter was inside the material at the change (Z {z}) – Z stays up, the program moves down itself.
ws.title: Workshop (dust extractor, compressor …)
ws.intro: Switch devices on smart plugs automatically: on when a job starts, off after the run-on time when it ends (done, stopped or disconnected). Errors never affect the job.
ws.presetTip: Template for the new device – replace “IP” with the address of your plug.
ws.kindTip: HTTP (Shelly, Tasmota, Home Assistant webhook) or MQTT (broker)
ws.enabledTip: Switch this device with the job
ws.none: No devices yet – choose a template and click “Add device”.
ws.onUrlTip: Called when the job starts. Only http:// (devices in your own network).
ws.onBodyTip: Sent with POST/PUT (e.g. JSON). Empty = no text.
ws.offUrlTip: Called after the run-on time when the job has ended.
ws.offBodyTip: Sent with POST/PUT (e.g. JSON). Empty = no text.
ws.tokenTip: Sent as “Authorization: Bearer …” (e.g. Home Assistant long-lived token). Never shown in the console.
ws.hostTip: Address of the MQTT broker (e.g. Mosquitto, Home Assistant).
ws.userTip: MQTT user name – empty if the broker needs no login.
ws.passwordTip: MQTT password. Never shown in the console.
ws.delayTip: How long the device keeps running after the job ends (e.g. 30 s for the dust extractor). A new job in this time keeps it on.
ws.err.https-not-supported: https is not supported – use http:// (devices in your own network)
ws.err.auth-not-supported: addresses with user:password@ are not supported – use a token
ws.err.mqtt-bad-answer: no MQTT broker at this address
cam.avoidCutTip: Rapid moves (G0) go around parts and holes that are already cut (bounding box + margin) instead of straight over them – tipped-up pieces could otherwise hit the head. If nothing is in the way, the move stays straight
cam.optOrderTip: Cuts the contours of each layer in the order with the shortest rapid moves (nearest neighbour + 2-opt). Holes and everything inside a part still come before the part; layer order and pierce points stay. On the laser, the start point of closed contours without lead-in may move
gc.orderOpt: cut order optimized: rapids {a} mm -> {b} mm
vfd.title: Spindle inverter (Modbus)
vfd.intro: Control the spindle directly at the inverter – through an RS-485 USB adapter (Modbus RTU) or over the network (Modbus TCP). First set the inverter's command and frequency source to “communication/RS-485”. Always check the registers in your own inverter manual!
vfd.linkTip: RS-485 through a USB adapter (Modbus RTU) or network (Modbus TCP).
vfd.portTip: Serial port of the RS-485 USB adapter.
vfd.parityTip: Must match the inverter setting (often 8N1 or 8E1).
vfd.hostTip: IP address of the inverter or Modbus gateway. Without a port, 502 is used.
vfd.unitTip: Modbus address of the inverter (1–247), set in the inverter.
vfd.profileTip: Register map of the inverter. If none fits, choose “Custom profile” and enter the registers from the manual.
vfd.maxRpmTip: Spindle speed at maximum frequency, e.g. 24000.
vfd.maxHzTip: Frequency at maximum speed, e.g. 400 Hz.
vfd.mapHint: Assumed registers of the profile. Compare them with the manual! Values as 0x2000 (hex) or decimal.
vfd.r.controlTip: Register that receives the forward/reverse/stop command.
vfd.r.fwdTip: Value in the control word for “run forward”.
vfd.r.revTip: Value in the control word for “run reverse”.
vfd.r.stopTip: Value in the control word for “stop”.
vfd.r.actualTip: Register for the output frequency/actual speed (empty = don't read).
vfd.r.faultTip: Register with the fault code (empty = don't read, 0 = no fault).
vfd.copyTip: Copy this profile and change the registers yourself.
vfd.fault: Fault: code {code} – see the inverter manual
vfd.rpmTip: Target speed sent to the inverter.
vfd.err.timeout: No answer (timeout). Check cable A/B, address, baud rate and parity.
vfd.err.crc: Corrupted answer (checksum wrong). Check cable, termination resistor and baud rate.
vfd.err.exception: Inverter refuses (code {code}): register or value does not fit – check the profile.
vfd.err.frame: Answer does not match the request – check device address and profile.
vfd.err.range: Max. speed and max. frequency must be greater than 0.
vfd.err.custom: Custom profile: control word, setpoint and the three command values must be filled in.
vfd.log.noTarget: Inverter: choose a port or address first.
vfd.log.help: Tip: set Modbus/RS-485 as command and frequency source in the inverter, compare address/baud rate/parity and swap RS-485 A and B if needed.
m.ruidaUsbNone: no port found – plug in the cable, switch the laser on, then 🔄
cyc.expanded: Drilling cycles: {n} holes converted into plain G0/G1 moves ({lines} lines will be sent).
cyc.tapWarn: ⚠ Tapping ({n}×): GRBL cannot sync the spindle with the feed – use a floating tap holder (length compensation) only! At the bottom it reverses with M4 to back out.
cyc.refused: Job not started – drilling cycle in line {n} cannot be converted: {line} – {why}
cyc.err.incremental: Cycles with G91 (incremental) are not supported – please post with G90.
cyc.err.rBelowZ: Hole depth Z is above the retract plane R.
cyc.err.dwellMs: Dwell P over 60 s – probably given in milliseconds. Switch the post processor to seconds.
cyc.err.unknownZ: Start height unknown (e.g. after G28) – move to a Z height before the cycle or use G99.
tl.typeTip.threadmill: Mills internal and external threads on a helical path. Angle = flank angle (metric 60°), plus the pitch. Not for normal contours.
tl.pitchTip: Thread pitch in mm, e.g. 1 for M6, 1.25 for M8, 1.5 for M10.
ops.threadLenTip: How deep the thread goes (negative, from the top). The core hole must be at least this deep.
ops.threadDTip: Nominal Ø, e.g. 8 for M8. 0 = automatic from the circle: for holes via the core hole (6.8 mm → M8), for studs the circle Ø.
ops.threadLeftTip: Mill a left-hand instead of a right-hand thread.
gcw.threadTool: Shape {n}: thread milling needs a thread mill (tool type “Thread mill”) – skipped.
gcw.threadCircle: Shape {n}: thread milling only works on circles – skipped.
gcw.threadSide: Shape {n}: thread milling needs a hole (inside/pocket/drill) or a stud (outside) as first operation – skipped.
gcw.thread.pitch: Shape {n}: the thread mill has no pitch – skipped.
gcw.thread.length: Shape {n}: thread length is missing – skipped.
gcw.thread.toolTooBig: Shape {n}: thread mill Ø{d} is too big for this thread – skipped.
gcw.thread.toolNoFit: Shape {n}: thread mill Ø{d} does not fit into the core hole – skipped.
gcw.thread.small: Shape {n}: thread Ø is too small for the pitch – skipped.
gcw.threadCore: Shape {n}: the hole (Ø{h}) is only milled as an “Inside” contour – with the Ø{d} cutter a core stays in the middle and the thread mill would hit it. Choose “Pocket” as first operation.
tl.singleTip: One tooth at the bottom, cuts any pitch (e.g. single-profile solid carbide thread mill). The pitch then comes from the operation or the ISO coarse thread. “Flute length” = shoulder length L1 (how deep the neck reaches).
tl.neckTip: Ø of the neck behind the tooth (D3 in catalogues).
ops.threadPitchTip: Pitch in mm. 0 = automatic: ISO coarse thread for single-tooth mills (M8 → 1.25), otherwise the pitch of the tool. Enter it yourself for fine threads.
ops.threadPassesTip: How often the tool goes round the thread, a bit deeper each time – protects small tools (aluminium: 2–3).
ops.threadSpringTip: Run the last path once more at the end – smooths the flanks.
gcw.threadReach: Shape {n}: the thread is {l} mm long but the neck of the single-tooth mill only reaches {r} mm – the shank would hit.
lib.io.fusionSkipped: Fusion 360: {n} entries skipped (holders, probes, taps or similar – not available in CNC Craft).
